headline: Meta pauses employee tracking program after internal data leak
summary: Sensitive employee data, including private conversations and performance metrics, was inadvertently exposed to the entire Meta staff due to the AI program.
details: Meta has temporarily halted its controversial AI training program, the Model Capability Initiative (MCI), which tracked employee keystrokes and mouse movements. The suspension comes not from privacy concerns or worker backlash, but from an internal data leak that exposed sensitive information.

The leak, reported by Business Insider, made private employee conversations, performance data, and transcriptions accessible to all Meta employees. This incident raises further questions about Meta's handling of employee data and AI security.

A Meta spokesperson stated that while they have no indication of improper access, the company is pausing the program to conduct an investigation. This follows previous AI-related security incidents for Meta, including an agentic AI breach and hackers exploiting a customer service chatbot to hijack Instagram accounts.

The MCI program was designed with privacy safeguards, according to Meta. However, the incident suggests that the data collected was not as tightly controlled as previously claimed, leading to a significant internal exposure of sensitive employee information.

topic: mysterious repeating radio signals from space identified
headline_marked: Mysterious Repeating Radio Signals From Space [[Source Identified]]
headline: Mysterious Repeating Radio Signals From Space Source Identified
summary: Astronomers have pinpointed the origin of long-period radio transients (LPTs) to a white dwarf actively pulling material from a companion red dwarf star.
details: For the first time, an international research team has identified the source of mysterious repeating radio signals from space, known as long-period radio transients (LPTs). These signals, observed as bursts repeating at intervals from minutes to hours, have puzzled scientists for years.

Using the Australian Square Kilometer Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) radio telescope, researchers focused on an object named ASKAP J174508.9-505149. They confirmed through spectroscopic observations that it is a binary system where a white dwarf is actively accreting matter from a companion red dwarf star.

This white dwarf-red dwarf binary system orbits each other at an extremely close distance, with an orbital period of approximately 1.368 hours, closely matching the repetition period of the radio pulses. The companion star is estimated to be about 0.13 times the size and 0.096 times the mass of the sun.

The powerful radio bursts are believed to be generated in the region where the magnetic fields of the two stars interact. Simultaneously, the accretion process heats the gas, causing it to emit X-rays, though the radio and X-ray emissions originate from different locations within the system.

This discovery provides the strongest evidence to date that white dwarf-red dwarf binaries are a source of LPTs. Previous hypotheses included magnetars, but this finding offers a more concrete explanation supported by observational data.
